draft.title: Alkanes, alkenes and alkynes
card: Alkane
a hydrocarbon with only single bonds between carbon atoms. It is saturated, so each carbon holds as many hydrogen atoms as it can. Its names end in -ane, such as propane.
Alkene
a hydrocarbon with at least one carbon to carbon double bond. It is unsaturated. Its names end in -ene, such as propene.
Alkyne
a hydrocarbon with at least one carbon to carbon triple bond. It is also unsaturated. Its names end in -yne, such as propyne.

For chains with one double or triple bond and no rings, the general formulae are CnH2n+2 for alkanes, CnH2n for alkenes and CnH2n-2 for alkynes. A double or triple bond means fewer hydrogen atoms for the same number of carbons.
draft.remember: The bond between carbons sets the family: single is alkane, double is alkene, triple is alkyne.

a.q: A hydrocarbon has the molecular formula C4H8 and one double bond in its chain. Which family does it belong to?
opts: Alkene
Alkane
Alkyne
Saturated hydrocarbon
a.why: A double bond between carbons makes it an alkene, and C4H8 fits CnH2n. It is not an alkane, because an alkane has only single bonds and would be C4H10.
a.clue: Look at the type of bond between the carbon atoms.

b.q: A chain hydrocarbon with one multiple bond has 5 carbon atoms and 8 hydrogen atoms. Which statement is correct?
opts: It is an alkyne, because it fits CnH2n-2
It is an alkene, because it fits CnH2n
It is an alkane, because it fits CnH2n+2
It is an alkane, because it has 5 carbon atoms
b.why: With n = 5, CnH2n-2 gives C5H8, so the formula fits an alkyne with a triple bond. An alkene with 5 carbons would be C5H10, and an alkane would be C5H12.
b.clue: Work out what 2n-2 gives when n is 5.

b.best: It is an alkyne, because it fits CnH2n-2

problems.detail: The clue 'Work out what 2n-2 gives when n is 5' points straight at the alkyne formula, so it gives the answer away instead of making students test each formula.

The question states the compound has a double bond and asks for its family, so it is pure recall and very easy for Year 12. The formula C4H8 adds nothing, and the clue only restates what the question already says.
